newsitem.title: THAILAND: Credit Lyonnais sells stake in Thai finance firm.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais sells stake in Thai finance firm.

text.p: Thailand's ailing CL Sahaviriya Finance and Securities Co Ltd plans to sell half of the firm to undisclosed foreign buyers after Credit Lyonnais sold its stake, a senior company executive said on Friday.

"We will double our capital to 1.2 billion baht ($40.6 million) from 600 million and sell the whole capital increase shares to foreign investors," Managing Director Savin Chatsuwan told reporters. He declined to say which foreign investors were involved.
But he said French bank Credit Lyonnais had sold its 25 percent equity stake in the company.

CL Sahavirya is one of 16 ailing finance and securities houses closed by the central bank last month and given 14 days to announce mergers, find foreign buyers, or face absorption into stronger firms. The deadline expires on Friday.
The Bank of Thailand is promoting consolidation among the 91 firm Thai finance and securities industry to bolster confidence in the hard hit sector.
The industry is struggling to cope with declining revenues, high funding costs and a deterioratioon in asset quality as Thailand goes through its worst economic downturn for more than a decade.

Another ailing firm, Country Finance Co Ltd, said it would increase its registered capital to 1.3 billion baht from 640 million baht. Existing major shareholder Laem Thong Bank Plc had pledged to subscribe to the shares but foreign brokers were also involved, bank executives said.

Another ailing firm, Sub Thamrong Finance Co Ltd, had been unable to find foreign buyers or potential merger partners and would be absorbed into one of the five large finance and securities firms chosen by the central bank to head consolidation in the sector.
